newsitem.title: FRANCE: New government seen overhauling French media law.
newsitem.headline: New government seen overhauling French media law.

text.p: A left-wing French government, expected to be named later on Wednesday or on Thursday morning, is expected to overhaul the country's media law, according to the newspaper Le Monde.

It said the Socialists would change the "Carignon law", named after a former communications minister, that raised the limit on stakes in television companies held by private firms to 49 percent and awarded broadcast licences for 10 years.
The paper added that the planned merger between public television broadcasters Arte and La Septieme would go through.
But a 1996 deal tying the French public broadcasters exclusively to the TPS digital satellite service for three years "will almost certainly be abandoned".
TPS is operated by TF1, in which Bouygues owns 39 percent. It rivals Canalsatellite, which is run by pay television group Canal Plus.
Le Monde said two Socialist deputies proposed legislation in March to bring the maximum stake in television companies owned by a single private group back to 25 percent.
Generale des Eaux, through its 30 percent stake in Havas, controls Canal Plus. Rival utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux has a stake in M6.

TF1 is the biggest private broadcaster in France, rivalling state-owned France 2 and France 3 for audiences. Canal Plus is encrypted while M6 caters for smaller audiences. Arte and La Septieme are focused on culture, with Arte being Franco-German.
On the Paris bourse, dealers said a Socialist government's media policy was expected to hurt TF1 and boost Canal Plus.
TF1 has been supportive of centre-right governments. Canal Plus was founded by Andre Rousselet after French president Francois Mitterrand sought more television channels in the country.

At midday, TF1 shares were up 2.89 percent at 570 francs ($97.65), Bouygues was down 0.39 percent at 507 francs, Canal Plus up 3.51 percent at 1,032, Havas up 2.31 percent at 398.90 and M6 up 2.06 percent at 545. The blue-chip index was up 0.60 percent at 2640.31. ($ = 5.837 French Francs)
